title: Stream-lease renegotiation and idempotent chunk claims for SSE reconnects
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Introduce a lease-based reconnect protocol extension that lets clients and servers renegotiate chunk ownership after network interruptions. The goal is to enable safe retry/reconnect flows without producing duplicate semantic effects (e.g., duplicate function/tool calls or duplicated structured output records) while preserving low-latency delivery for streaming responses.
background: Current SSE resume mechanisms at Redwood rely on resume tokens and sequence windows, but we observed a class of duplication/forking issues when clients reconnect from different network paths, when intermediate proxies replay events, or when tool-calling frames straddle reconnect boundaries. Existing endpoints sometimes double-invoke tool functions or emit duplicate JSONL lines for structured outputs, causing downstream consumer confusion and billing noise.
proposal: Add an explicit 'stream lease' token and per-chunk claim header. The server issues a lease token on stream start (lease_id + expiry_ms). Each chunk delivered includes a chunk_id and an incremental claim_offset. On reconnect the client presents: last_applied_chunk_id and the lease_id it previously held. Server will validate whether that lease is still active; if expired, server will attempt lease-renegotiation by offering a new lease and optionally providing a compact 'ownership map' snapshot describing which chunk_ids are durable/accepted. Server will respond with a reconnect decision: resume_from chunk_id X (idempotent replay), replay_range, or full-restart. To protect function/tool call atomicity, the server marks function-call chunks as 'atomic' in the ownership map; the server will never replay partial atomic chunk frames across lease boundaries. Clients must prefer server-declared canonical boundaries to avoid duplicate tool invocations.
api_changes:
- stream_start response includes: lease_id (string), lease_ttl_ms (int), server_epoch (string)
- each SSE data chunk includes headers: chunk_id, claim_offset, atomic_flag (true/false), resume_hint (optional)
- reconnect request: POST /streams/{stream_id}/reconnect with body: {lease_id?, last_applied_chunk_id?} (legacy resume token accepted for backward compatibility)
- reconnect response: {decision: 'resume'|'replay'|'restart', resume_from_chunk_id?, new_lease_id?}
server_behavior:
- Issue lease at stream open; persist leases short-term in runtime memory with write-ahead to raft log for short retention window.
- When client reconnects, validate incoming lease_id: if matches active lease and last_applied_chunk_id <= latest_chunk_id then allow fast resume and mark any in-flight chunks as completed.
- If lease conflict or expiry: attempt lease-renegotiation. If another client is concurrently claiming ownership, resolve deterministically by server_epoch.
- Do not split atomic function-call chunks across reconnect decisions. If reconnect would cut inside an atomic chunk, server will choose to restart or replay from the previous atomic boundary.
- Provide a compact ownership snapshot for large gaps if client lost many chunks; snapshot is optional and gated by a feature flag to limit memory and bandwidth.
client_behavior:
- Include last_applied_chunk_id and previous lease_id when reconnecting.
- If the server responds with 'resume', rehydrate KV cache and continue token consumption.
- If the server responds with 'replay', accept duplicate chunks up to resume_from and deduplicate based on chunk_id. For atomic chunks, client must defer emitting function call side effects until server confirms atomic completion.
- If 'restart', reset local partial outputs and re-issue top-level request if idempotency key allowed, otherwise surface explicit error to caller.
edge_cases:
- Split atomic chunk appears: server must not resume inside atomic; choose replay/restart.
- Concurrent reconnects from multi-device sessions: server_epoch and lease ownership map break ties; older leases are preempted with a controlled grace window.
- Large-gap reconnect where ownership snapshot is not available: server will return 'restart' and include guidance for client-side retry semantics.
- Proxy replay: chunk_id+lease_id pair prevents accidental double-acceptance when proxies replay past fragments (server ignores replays older than last_durable_chunk), but still logs duplicate attempts for debugging.
acceptance_criteria:
- Clients can reconnect and resume with <1% duplicate function-call invocations in fault-injection tests.
- Latency regression for steady-state streaming <5% after enabling lease headers.
- Telemetry emits lease_acquired, lease_expired, reconnect_decision events and counts.
- Backwards compatibility: legacy clients using resume_token still supported with server-side translation layer.
- Integration tests covering: normal reconnect, expired lease, concurrent claim, atomic chunk boundary handling.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for chunk_id generation, atomic_flag handling, and claim_offset monotonicity.
- Integration tests with fault-injection harness that cuts TCP mid-chunk and replays fragments.
- Chaos tests across nodes to validate lease preemption and server_epoch resolution.
- End-to-end customer-sim tests where a tool-call stub asserts single invocation semantics.
- Load tests to ensure ownership snapshot generation does not degrade throughput.
metrics_and_alerts:
- Metrics: lease_issue_rate, lease_renew_rate, lease_expiry_rate, reconnect_success_rate, duplicate_chunk_rate, duplicate_toolcall_rate.
- Alerts: duplicate_toolcall_rate > 0.5% for 10m, reconnect_success_rate < 99% for 15m, lease_store_pressure > 80%.
rollout_plan:
- Feature gate via runtime flag 'stream_lease' default off.
- Phase 1: internal Canary against canary accounts for 24h.
- Phase 2: opt-in beta for selected customers with known reconnect patterns.
- Phase 3: gradual enable by region and model tier, monitor metrics and roll back if duplicate_toolcall_rate spikes.
- Full release after 2 weeks of stable metrics and green integration test runs.
notes: Consider adding compact ownership bloom filters if snapshot sizes become large.
